title: company-wide-policies-and-processes-2026-06-15
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document centralizes Redwood Inference company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates used by teams. It is intended for all employees and provides the authoritative process, owners, and links to forms and templates.

Quick reference (owners and SLAs)

- Access & permissions owner: Security (security@redwood.com) — SLA for standard role changes: 3 business days; emergency access: 4 hours.
- Change management owner: Eng Platform (platform@redwood.com) — Emergency change window: 24/7; regular changes: scheduled weekly change window.
- Data management owner: Data Governance (datagov@redwood.com) — Data retention exceptions processed within 10 business days.
- Procurement & expenses owner: Finance (procurement@redwood.com / expenses@redwood.com) — PO approvals within 5 business days.
- Vendor management owner: Legal & Procurement (vendors@redwood.com) — Third-party assessments within 15 business days.
- Travel owner: People Ops (travel@redwood.com) — Reimbursement processed within 10 business days after complete submission.

1) Access and permissions

Purpose: Provide a repeatable, auditable process for granting, reviewing, and revoking access to systems and data. Scope: all employee and contractor access to cloud consoles, internal apps, production systems, and PII/regulated datasets.

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Timebound access for contractors and short-lived projects.
- Separation of duties for privileged operations.

Process (standard requests):
1. Requestor opens an Access Request ticket via the internal IT portal and selects the appropriate role template (e.g., "developer-gcp-basic", "infra-operator", "data-analyst-sensitive").
2. Requestor provides justification and desired duration.
3. Manager approval required (automatic workflow).
4. Security team performs role mapping and approves within SLA.
5. Access is provisioned and logged; request is closed.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Submit a high-priority ticket with incident reference and obtain manager + on-call security approval.
- Access granted is explicitly timebound (default 4 hours) and audited; retrospective review required within 3 business days.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly review for high-privilege groups (admins, infra ops, DBAs).
- Annual access re-certification for application owners (owners receive a report and must attest).

Service accounts and keys:
- Service accounts must follow lifecycle rules: rotate keys every 90 days, avoid long-lived keys where possible, and use workload identity federation for cloud services.

2) Change management

Purpose: Reduce risk of outages and data loss by standardizing how changes are planned, tested, reviewed, and executed. Scope: all production-facing changes, infra provisioning, and schema migrations.

Change types and approvals:
- Standard changes: Pre-approved low-risk changes (e.g., configuration tweaks) — submit via Change Request form; notification to stakeholders required 48 hours prior.
- Normal changes: Require CAB review (weekly CAB meeting) and change plan with rollback.
- Emergency changes: Documented in post-implementation review (PIR); notification within 2 hours post-change.

Required artifacts for normal changes:
- Change Request Form (title, owner, risk level, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window).
- Runbook excerpt showing key validation steps.
- Pre-deployment checklist: automated tests green, canary plan defined, monitoring alerts in place.

Execution checklist (example):
1. Confirm change window with stakeholders.
2. Run pre-deploy tests and snapshot critical state (DB backup or config export).
3. Deploy to canary subset and validate metrics for 30 minutes (latency, error rate, token throughput).
4. Gradually roll out, monitoring SLOs (error rate < 0.5%, p99 latency < target).
5. If rollback criteria met, execute rollback plan and notify CAB.

3) Data management

Purpose: Ensure proper handling, classification, retention, and deletion of company data and customer data in line with regulatory and contractual obligations.

Data classification levels:
- Public: non-sensitive documentation and marketing material.
- Internal: company-internal notes and operational metrics.
- Confidential: PII, billing records, model training datasets with personal data.
- Restricted: regulated data (HIPAA/CCPA-related), customer production data under contract clauses.

Retention and deletion:
- Standard logs: retained 90 days in hot storage, archived 2 years.
- Audit logs: retained 7 years (for compliance evidence).
- Customer data: retention as per contract; default retention 1 year unless otherwise specified.
- Data deletion process: Data owners must submit a Data Deletion Request; DPO approves; operations executes deletion and verifies with cryptographic proof of deletion where applicable.

Data access controls:
- Sensitive datasets require ACLs + data access approvals via the Data Access Request workflow.
- Analytics copies must be anonymized or tokenized when moving outside secure enclaves.

Backup and DR:
- Critical metadata and config: snapshot every 24 hours, cross-region replication.
- RTO target: 4 hours for critical control plane services; RPO: 1 hour for in-flight KV caches.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals (summary table):
| Amount (USD) | Required approvals | Notes |
|--------------|--------------------|-------|
| <= 500       | Manager | Use corporate card or expense claim |
| 501 - 5,000  | Manager + Finance | Formal PO recommended for software/services |
| 5,001 - 50,000 | Director + Finance | Procurement involvement required |
| > 50,000     | VP + Procurement + Legal | Contract and PO mandatory |

Procurement process (software/infra purchases):
1. Fill the Purchase Requisition form with justification, vendor, and TCO estimate.
2. Obtain manager approval and submit to procurement@redwood.com. Procurement performs vendor check and compares at least 2 quotes for amounts > $5k.
3. Legal reviews contracts (SLA, data handling, liability).
4. Finance issues PO and routes to vendor.

Expense policy (travel & local expenses):
- Use the corporate travel portal for booking (preferred vendors have negotiated rates).
- Per diem and daily meal caps are defined in the travel template (see Templates section).
- Receipts required for any claim > $25. Attach scanned receipts via the expense portal.
- Fraudulent claims will be investigated and may result in disciplinary action.

5) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist for third parties:
- Vendor Risk Assessment (security questionnaire).
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) if processing customer data.
- Insurance certificates and proof of identity.
- Technical integration plan and escalation contacts.
- Role-based access (principle of least privilege) for vendor staff; timebound credentials.

Periodic reviews and KPIs:
- Annual security recertification for vendors with production access.
- Quarterly performance review for strategic vendors (uptime, responsiveness, incident count).

Termination and offboarding:
- Revoke all vendor credentials within 24 hours of contract termination.
- Perform data return or certified deletion per contract.

6) Travel policy

Booking and approvals:
- All international travel requires People Ops approval at least 10 business days prior.
- Managers must confirm travel purpose and budget in the Travel Request form.

Allowed expenses and limits:
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; Premium Economy or business requires Director approval.
- Hotel: standard business class rooms; negotiated vendor rates preferred.
- Ground transportation: rideshares or standard car services; pre-approval for rental cars.

Safety and duty of care:
- Register with People Ops for travel: travel@redwood.com. We provide emergency assistance and country risk briefings.
- Emergency medical coverage: company-provided policy details are on the Benefits page.

Expense submission steps:
1. Submit expense within 14 days of travel completion via the expense portal.
2. Attach itemized receipts and the approved Travel Request.
3. Manager approves; Finance issues reimbursement within 10 business days.

7) Internal templates and artifacts

Canonical templates (location: /confluence/templates and Google Drive /Company/Templates):
- Access Request template (access-request-form) — fields: requestor, role, justification, duration, manager.
- Change Request Form (change-request-template) — includes rollback plan and pre/post checks.
- Purchase Requisition (purchase-requisition-template).
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (vendor-onboarding-checklist).
- Travel Request and Expense template (travel-request-template).
- Data Deletion Request (data-deletion-request-template).

How to use templates:
- Copy the template page and replace placeholders. Keep one canonical page per template; minor team-specific extensions are allowed but must include a link back to the canonical template.

Governance, exceptions, and enforcement

- Exceptions: Teams may request an exception by submitting a Risk & Exception Request to risk-and-exceptions@redwood.com. Approved exceptions must include compensating controls and a defined review period.
- Noncompliance: Noncompliant behavior will be escalated to the owner_team and People Ops; repeated violations may result in revocation of privileges or disciplinary actions.
- Reviews: This document and the templates will be reviewed annually by People Ops, Security, and Finance. Ad-hoc reviews triggered by incidents or regulation changes will occur as needed.

Appendices

B. Example change request (YAML snippet)
---
title: "migrate-config-v2"
owner: "infra-team"
risk: "medium"
window: "2026-06-20T02:00:00Z"
rollback: "restore-config from snapshot-20260620"
validation_steps:
  - "smoke tests pass"
  - "p99 latency within baseline"
---

C. Links to templates and forms
- Access Request: /confluence/templates/access-request-form
- Change Request: /confluence/templates/change-request-template
- Purchase Requisition: /confluence/templates/purchase-requisition-template

Document change log:
